themes.theme: Hyperscaler AI capex still rising into 2027
themes.evidence: A July 2026 report has the largest cloud operators' combined 2026 capex up ~89% y/y to ~$710B (prior +72%); BofA (Arya) sees global cloud/AI infrastructure capex approaching $1.5T by 2027; TSMC lifted 2026 capex to $60-64B (Jul 2026). The GPU/custom-silicon leaders already price this in (MRVL at ~65x FY1/38x FY2 EPS, +287% off its 52w low; CIEN ~38x FY27). Sources: finance.yahoo.com semis $1.3T article (2026); news.ainauten.com chip-capex-doubt story (Jul 2026).

themes.theme: Value migrating to rack-scale integration and data-center power (EMS/ODM)
themes.evidence: Flex's Cloud and Power Infrastructure unit is guided to grow 65-75% in FY27 (Jul 29, 2026 call) and Flex sold $2.0B of preferred in it (Axiom) at a $37.5B EV on 2026-10-05, vs Flex's own EV of ~$46.6B. Sanmina's ZT Systems (bought from AMD Oct 2025) runs at a $5-6B annual rate, and management says FY27 revenue will exceed $16B. Both stocks sit 25-30% below their June 2026 highs even though guidance went up, so the market has not yet repriced them for this growth.

themes.theme: Advanced packaging, HBM and silicon photonics/optical interconnect
themes.evidence: Onto raised its 2026 advanced-packaging growth outlook to ~80% from 50%, has a >$1B backlog and won a >$200M Dragonfly order from one OSAT for 2027 delivery (Aug 6, 2026). Amkor expects advanced-packaging revenue to triple in 2026. GlobalFoundries' photonics-led data-center segment grew 62% y/y and is targeted to double in 2026, with a $1B run-rate exiting 2028. Semtech guides Q3 FY27 revenue +20% q/q on data-center ACC/LPO.

Gartner projects 2026 DRAM/NAND prices +125%/+234%, with relief not until late 2027. UBS sees DRAM undersupplied until at least 2Q28 (streetinsider, 2026). SNDK is +1183% on 12-1 momentum and WDC/MU have already re-rated. The second-order effect is negative for phone and PC demand: GFS guides its mobile segment down low-teens in 2026 and Qualcomm's China OEM demand is weak.

themes.theme: Semis volatility: AI-capex durability doubts and China equipment
themes.evidence: In late July 2026 the SOX fell into a bear market on AI-spend durability doubts and reports of Chinese state-backed tool production. KLAC fell >6% despite a beat (Jul 28-29, 2026; quiverquant, sentisense), GFS fell 34% from Jun 22 to Jul 21 (tickeron) and ONTO fell ~44% from its June high to its July low. Estimates kept rising through that selloff, which is where today's entry points come from.

themes.theme: Software: AI-agent seat-compression scare, then rebound to usage-priced names
themes.evidence: IGV fell ~30% in early 2026 on the 'SaaSpocalypse' (seat-based pricing fears), then rose ~42% from its April low by Jun 3 (Reuters via finance.yahoo.com, 2026-06-03). Security, observability and communications names have since run hard (OKTA +264%, CRWD +189%, TWLO +148%, NET +117% over 6 months) and now mostly trade above their average analyst targets, so I took no software picks. Data note: Alpha Vantage's daily limit was used up and Twelve Data estimates/statistics are plan-gated, so consensus estimates come from stockanalysis.com pages read with WebFetch (S&P Global data, 2026-10-09). Prices and monthly history come from Twelve Data quote/time_series. WebSearch worked throughout.

ideas.name: Flex Ltd.
ideas.thesis: Flex is spinning off Axiom, its Cloud and Power Infrastructure business, which is guided to grow 65-75% in FY27 (Mar-27) and accelerate further in FY28. A $2.0B preferred raise just valued Axiom at a $37.5B EV, which implies the rest of Flex (~$23B of revenue) trades at only ~$9B EV. Consensus EPS rises 43% in FY27 and 50% in FY28, while the stock is 29% below its June high at ~17x FY28 EPS.
ideas.why_now: On 2026-10-05 Flex agreed to sell $2.0B of Axiom convertible preferred to General Catalyst and Koch at a $37.5B initial EV. This is a third-party price for the spin-co before it trades. The Axiom Form 10 was filed 2026-09-15 (ticker AXM) and the spin is targeted for Q1 CY2027. FY27 guidance was raised on 2026-07-29 (revenue $33.7-35.2B from $32.3-33.8B; adj. EPS $4.42-4.74), yet the stock is still below its pre-earnings level.

catalysts.event: Q2 FY27 earnings (Q2 guide: revenue $7.95-8.25B, adj. EPS $1.00-1.07)
Investor Day: first long-term targets for Axiom and the remaining Flex
EPC Power acquisition expected to close in Q4 2026; Axiom preferred investment closes
Axiom spin-off completes (Q1 CY2027) and AXM begins trading

ideas.valuation: At $118.2: 25x FY27 consensus EPS ($4.71) and 16.7x FY28 ($7.06); stockanalysis lists a 22.7x forward P/E and 21.4x EV/EBITDA on trailing EBITDA. PEG ~0.5. Sum of the parts: Flex EV ~$46.6B minus the $37.5B Axiom mark leaves ~$9B for a ~$23B-revenue EMS business, roughly 0.4x sales. Flex traded around 10-15x forward EPS before 2025 (approximate, my own recollection, not verified this session). Net debt is $3.1B.
ideas.estimate_revisions: Up. FY27 guidance raised on 2026-07-29 (revenue midpoint $34.45B vs $33.41B Street; EPS midpoint $4.58 vs $4.53). FY27 consensus EPS is now $4.71 (range $4.60-4.96), above the guidance midpoint, and FY28 is $7.06 (+50%) (consensus updated 2026-09-28). Average target $160.5 (+36%), 11 analysts, all Buy or Strong Buy.
ideas.forward_growth: Consensus revenue +24% FY27 ($34.6B) and +30% FY28 ($45.0B); EPS +43% FY27 and +50% FY28 (stockanalysis/S&P Global, 2026-10-09). CPI segment (Axiom) guided +65-75% in FY27 after +38% in FY26 and +35% in Q1 FY27, which implies a steep second-half ramp.
ideas.priced_in: 6-month +76% (from ~$67 at the start of April to $118). +122% from the 52-week low (~$53, Nov 2025) but -29% from the $166.86 June high. The stock fell to $99.5 in July and has only partly recovered while FY27/FY28 estimates rose. The Axiom private mark implies the remaining Flex is valued near zero beyond a token multiple, and the stock has not re-rated toward that mark.
key_risks: Spin execution: Form 10 effectiveness, separation costs and dis-synergies; Flex guarantees a redemption premium (15-25%) if the spin slips past 2027-12-31
The preferred (10% cash dividend pre-spin, 6-7% after) is senior to common equity in Axiom, so the $37.5B EV overstates what accrues to Flex holders
AI data-center capex slowdown would hit the CPI ramp, which is concentrated in a few hyperscalers
The remaining Flex is low-margin, low-to-mid single-digit growth EMS; tariffs and consumer/auto weakness
ideas.overlap_with_holdings: Indirect AI data-center exposure shared with NVDA, AVGO, GOOGL, AMZN and VST (power), but the mechanism is different: power, cooling and rack integration rather than chips. JBL is a watchlist EMS peer, and SANM below is a sister idea.

ideas.name: Onto Innovation Inc.
ideas.thesis: Onto supplies process control (inspection and metrology) and lithography for advanced packaging (2.5D/CoWoS, HBM, panel). It is the most direct equipment play on packaging becoming the AI bottleneck, and its growth is accelerating: backlog is above $1B for the first time and a >$200M single-OSAT Dragonfly order delivers in 2027. At ~25x 2027 EPS with EPS growing 44%, it is cheaper than KLAC (~36x FY27 to Jun-27) while growing faster.
ideas.why_now: On 2026-08-06 Q2 beat the top of guidance on every line (record $343M revenue, EPS $1.93). Management raised its H2-over-H1 growth to >=25% from 15% and its 2026 advanced-packaging growth to ~80% from 50%, and guided Q3 to $380-400M and EPS $2.18-2.38. The stock is still 24% below its June high after the July semis selloff.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings (guide $380-400M, EPS $2.18-2.38) and Q4 outlook (mgmt says Q4 > Q3)
2027 outlook; deliveries of the >$200M OSAT Dragonfly order weighted to 2027
Panel-level packaging and HBM4 tool ramps

ideas.valuation: At $295: 36x 2026 EPS ($8.11) and 25x 2027 ($11.70); stockanalysis lists a 28.7x forward P/E and PEG 0.71. EV/EBITDA is 45x trailing but falls quickly on 2027 numbers. Peer comparison: KLAC is at 36x FY27 (Jun) and 29x FY28 EPS with slower growth (+45%/+23%). Net cash is $410M. Average target $387.5 (+31%), 12 analysts, all Buy or Strong Buy.
ideas.estimate_revisions: Up. 2026 EPS consensus is now $8.11 (+64% y/y, range $7.99-8.25) after H2 guidance was raised ~10 points (15% to >=25% H2/H1). The advanced-packaging outlook was lifted from +50% to +80%. Q2 EPS beat Zacks consensus by 15% (2026-08-06). Consensus updated 2026-10-02.
ideas.forward_growth: Consensus revenue +43% in 2026 ($1.44B) and +31% in 2027 ($1.88B); EPS +64% in 2026 and +44% in 2027 (stockanalysis/S&P Global, 2026-10-09). Backlog >$1B extends into 2027.
ideas.priced_in: 6-month +40% (~$210 at the start of April to $295). +148% from the 52-week low (~$119, Nov 2025) but -24% from the $386.46 June high. The stock round-tripped to $215 in July while estimates kept rising, so the 2027 EPS step-up (+44%) and the 2027-dated OSAT order are not yet reflected in a multiple that sits below KLAC's.
key_risks: Concentration in TSMC/OSAT CoWoS and HBM capacity adds; orders are lumpy
A semis/AI-capex sentiment selloff like July 2026; high beta
China export controls and Chinese domestic tool competition
High trailing multiple if the 2027 ramp slips
ideas.overlap_with_holdings: Tied to the NVDA/AVGO AI-accelerator build-out (CoWoS/HBM), so correlated with those holdings. AMAT, LRCX, FORM and CDNS on the watchlist are adjacent semicap names, but Onto is a packaging-specific niche.

ideas.name: Sanmina Corporation
ideas.thesis: The ZT Systems acquisition (from AMD, Oct 2025) turned Sanmina into a hyperscale rack-integration supplier. FY26 revenue is guided ~$14.1B (+74%) and management is 'increasingly confident' of >$16B in FY27, with second-half acceleration from new hyperscaler and OEM programs. The stock trades at 15.6x FY27 consensus EPS ($13.92), the cheapest multiple among the AI-exposed EMS names, and sits 25% below its June high.
ideas.why_now: Q3 FY26 (2026-07-27) revenue was $3.46B (+70% y/y), and FY26 EPS guidance was raised to $11.90-12.20 from $10.75-11.35. The stock still fell from $208.90 to $184 on the print (no buybacks; a Q2 pull-forward flattered H1) and has only recovered to ~$217. The FY27 guide on Nov 2 is the next test.

catalysts.event: Q4 FY26 earnings and first formal FY27 outlook (>$16B revenue framework)
New hyperscaler rack programs ramp; ZT at the $5-6B annual framework

ideas.valuation: At $217: 15.6x FY27 consensus EPS ($13.92), 18x FY26 guidance midpoint ($12.05); stockanalysis lists a 16.7x forward P/E, 14.1x EV/EBITDA, 0.78x forward P/S and PEG 0.61. That is a discount to FLEX (25x FY27/16.7x FY28) and to the AI-EMS group. Before ZT, Sanmina traded around 10-13x forward (approximate, my own recollection, not verified this session). Net debt is modest at $580M.
ideas.estimate_revisions: Up, but stale. The FY26 EPS guidance midpoint rose ~8% (from $11.05 to $12.05) at Q3. Sidoti lifted FY27 EPS to $11.57 from $10.24 (2026-07-31). FY27 consensus is now $13.92 (+15%) on revenue of $16.41B (+16%), but the consensus was last updated 2026-07-28 and only 4 analysts cover the stock, so Nov 2 guidance can move it materially. Average target $260 (+20%).
ideas.forward_growth: Consensus FY26 (Sep) revenue +74% and EPS +100%; FY27 revenue +16% and EPS +15% (stockanalysis/S&P Global). Its 3-year forecast growth is revenue +31%/yr and EPS +38%/yr. Management targets >$16B FY27 revenue with a back-half ramp, which looks conservative relative to ZT's $5-6B run-rate plus new wins.
ideas.priced_in: 6-month +66% (~$131 at the start of April to $217). +84% from the $118.10 52-week low but -25% from the $288.68 June 3 high. The stock dropped ~35% into July/August and has since recovered only partway. A 15-16x multiple on rising EPS implies the market treats ZT as low-quality, non-recurring revenue.
key_risks: Customer concentration in AMD-based racks and a few hyperscalers (JPMorgan Neutral flags this)
Thin EMS margins (~7% operating) and working-capital swings; Q2 orders were pulled forward
Thin coverage (4 analysts) and low float liquidity cause big moves on prints
Capital return was absent in Q3 (no buybacks despite ~$600M authorization)
ideas.overlap_with_holdings: Indirect AI-rack exposure correlated with NVDA, AVGO, GOOGL and AMZN capex. JBL on the watchlist is a direct EMS peer, and FLEX above is a sister idea, so pick one of the two if diversification matters.

ideas.name: GlobalFoundries Inc.
ideas.thesis: GlobalFoundries is a US/EU specialty foundry whose fastest-growing business, silicon photonics and SiGe for optical networking, grew 62% y/y and is targeted to double in 2026 and reach a $1B run-rate exiting 2028. Consensus has EPS growth accelerating to +34% in 2027. The stock has halved from its May high, so it now trades at 18x 2027 EPS and 12.9x EV/EBITDA with $1.6B net cash.
ideas.why_now: After a 60% YTD run to $92.55 (May 26), the stock lost ~48% on profit-taking, insider selling, the July semis rout and a soft mobile outlook. Meanwhile Q2 beat on revenue and EPS ($0.46; gross margin 29.9%), the data-center outlook was raised, and Commerce signed a $300M CHIPS LOI for photonics. The stock is now flat over 6 months even though 2027 EPS consensus is +34%.

catalysts.event: Q4 results and 2027 outlook, including photonics doubling and margin path
Target of a $1B photonics revenue run-rate exiting 2028

ideas.valuation: At $47.6: 24x 2026 EPS ($1.96) and 18x 2027 ($2.63); stockanalysis lists a 22.0x forward P/E, 12.85x EV/EBITDA and PEG 0.86, with net cash of $1.63B. Consensus target $74.68 (+57%) from 23 analysts (13 Buy or Strong Buy). The stock is now below its 200-day average ($54.55), whereas analog/specialty semis peers trade at 25-35x.
ideas.estimate_revisions: Flat to modestly up. Consensus was updated 2026-10-09: 2026 EPS $1.96 (range $1.86-2.10, +14%) and 2027 $2.63 (+34%). Q2 beat consensus and the data-center/photonics outlook was raised. Upgrades came in May-June 2026 (Cantor to Overweight with an $80 target, Arete to Buy, Susquehanna Positive with a $100 target). The drag is the mobile segment (36% of revenue), guided down low-teens on memory-price-driven handset weakness.
ideas.forward_growth: Consensus revenue +7.6% in 2026 ($7.31B) and +12.5% in 2027 ($8.22B); EPS +14% and +34% (stockanalysis/S&P Global, 2026-10-09). The mix shifts toward photonics/data center (16% of revenue at +62% y/y), which lifts margins.
ideas.priced_in: 6-month -2% (screen); -48.5% from the $92.55 52-week high and +49% from the $32.02 low. The selloff erased the entire photonics re-rating while 2027 EPS growth of +34% and the CHIPS photonics award stayed intact, so the market is pricing GFS as a mature-node commodity foundry again.
key_risks: Mobile weakness (36% of revenue) from memory-driven handset cost inflation could persist into 2027
Chinese mature-node overcapacity (China capacity +14% in 2025) pressures pricing
Mubadala/insider selling overhang

Photonics is still small (~$290M/quarter) and the targets are management aspirations; some government contract exposure (CHIPS, a $3.1B DoD trusted-foundry contract), though most revenue is commercial
ideas.overlap_with_holdings: Low overlap: GFS does not make leading-edge AI accelerators (NVDA/AVGO use TSMC). Its exposures are optical networking, auto, industrial and mobile, which diversifies the portfolio's AI-compute concentration. Partial thematic overlap with LITE, AAOI and CRDO on the watchlist, which are photonics/interconnect customers rather than competitors.

ideas.name: Semtech Corporation
ideas.thesis: Semtech's data-center business (ACC active copper cables, LPO/optical drivers, CopperEdge) is inflecting: Q3 FY27 is guided to $410M revenue (+20% q/q) and $1.05 EPS versus $0.71 in Q2 and $0.48 a year ago, with record backlog. Consensus has EPS +103% in FY27 and +68% in FY28, so at ~32x FY28 EPS the multiple is reasonable for the growth, even though the stock has already run.
ideas.why_now: On 2026-08-25 Q2 FY27 beat guidance (revenue $341.9M vs $328M guide; EPS $0.71 vs $0.61), and Q3 was guided sharply higher with gross margin stepping to 58.3%. The low-margin cellular module business is classified as held for sale (63.9% gross margin ex-modules), which will clean up the mix.

catalysts.event: Q3 FY27 earnings (guide $410M, EPS $1.05) and Q4 outlook
Hyperscaler ACC/LPO ramps at 1.6T; close of the cellular-module sale

ideas.valuation: At $186.8: 54x FY27 (Jan-27) EPS ($3.48) and 32x FY28 ($5.86); stockanalysis lists a 37.8x forward P/E. Annualizing the Q3 EPS guide ($1.05 x 4 = $4.20) gives ~44x run-rate. Interconnect peers (CRDO, ALAB on the watchlist) trade at higher multiples. Net debt is $321M. Average target $214.6 (+15%), consensus Strong Buy (16 analysts).
ideas.estimate_revisions: Up. Q2 beat its own EPS guidance by 16% and the Q3 guide implies +48% q/q EPS. FY27 consensus is now $3.48 (range $3.37-3.69) and FY28 $5.86 (consensus updated 2026-10-09). Price targets were raised after the August print (UBS to $230, per an undated report; I could not confirm the year).
ideas.forward_growth: Consensus revenue +42% in FY27 ($1.49B) and +30% in FY28 ($1.93B); EPS +103% and +68% (stockanalysis/S&P Global, 2026-10-09). Data-center growth was guided >50% organic for FY27 (Mar 2026 Roth conference).
ideas.priced_in: Already moved a lot: 6-month +120%, 52-week +164%, 5% below the 52-week high (screen). The case for more upside rests on the FY28 EPS step-up (+68%) and margin mix after the module sale. It is a lower-conviction pick because momentum, not price lag, describes it today.
key_risks: Valuation and positioning after a +164% year; short interest 7.3% of float
ACC vs AEC competition (Credo) and hyperscaler program concentration
Execution of the cellular-module divestiture; net debt
AI-capex sentiment swings (July 2026 rout)
ideas.overlap_with_holdings: Correlated with the NVDA/AVGO AI networking build-out and thematically close to watchlist names CRDO, ALAB, LITE and AAOI, so it adds little diversification.
